# Bank Transfer Process Clause

Defines a conditional policy for requesting one bank transfer within a Bank Transfer Contract. `paymentPolicyAction` is `transfer`. A request records intent; only a bank confirmation records transferred money. Unknown outcomes reconcile against the same request. There is no synthetic card authorization or capture, and a refund requires a separate transfer instruction.

## Configuration

Parameters are read from the clause instance in the executing document (`readParametersFromDocument: true`). Execution requires a Bank Transfer Contract.

- `parameters.method` accepts `bank-transfer` or `conditional-bank`, defaulting to `bank-transfer`.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to `{}`. Its `mode` accepts `workflow` or `when`, defaulting to `workflow`.
- `workflow` mode retains connection planning without adding the automatic conditional request machinery described below.
- `when` mode requires `parameters.transfer.when` and a nonempty text `parameters.transfer.requestId`. Requests additionally enforce a maximum request ID length of 128 characters.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to `{}` and declares source aliases used by the condition. Every `/sources/<alias>/...` reference must name a declared alias.

The condition permits `$document`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract`, and `$literal`, with `list` and `val` operand fields. `$document` references must be static absolute paths other than `/`. Literal contents are not scanned. Traversal is bounded to levels 0–32; deeper expressions and unsupported operators are rejected.

Policy transitions are rejected with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

## Conditional requests

In `when` mode, the clause initializes `/paymentProcess_<clauseKey>/transferAllowed` to `false` and sets `/paymentTerms/transferGate` to that path. An existing different gate is rejected. Paths refer to the document where the clause executes, including a nested instruction’s own document.

The gate becomes true only when `/activation/active` is exactly `true`, the condition evaluates to exactly `true`, and either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly `true`. Changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks`, and condition-referenced paths trigger reevaluation. Declared sources also add an embedded-source event handler.

After reevaluation, an automatic request is attempted only when the gate is true, `/payment/accepted` is exactly `true`, `/payment/closed` is exactly `false`, and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. It uses the configured `requestId` and event execution mode, which bypasses the payer-channel check. A true gate means the condition allows a request, not that money has moved.

The contract’s `requestTransfer` operation instead requires the calling channel to match `/paymentTerms/payerChannel`. Both request routes require acceptance and, when document sources are configured, source readiness. Request input permits only `requestId`.

After those checks, an already-recorded matching ID returns `duplicate`; a different ID is rejected. This duplicate check precedes the closed-payment and transfer-gate checks. A new request is rejected if `/payment/closed` is `true` or an existing `/paymentTerms/transferGate` does not resolve to exactly `true`. An accepted new request stores `/bankTransfer/requestId`, sets `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested`, and emits a Bank Transfer Event with `kind: Transfer Requested`, `requestId`, `amountMinor`, and `currency` from `/paymentTerms`. `acceptedNew` confirms request recording only.

## Bank outcomes and amounts

`confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer`, and `reportTransferUnknown` report `completed`, `declined`, and `unknown`, respectively. The calling channel must match `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel`. Outcome input permits only `requestId`, `reference`, `amountMinor`, and `currency`; the ID must match the recorded nonempty request, and `reference` must be nonempty text of at most 256 characters.

Confirmation requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to equal `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` and `/paymentTerms/currency`. Amounts are integer minor units of that currency. This records the full instruction amount, not a partial transfer or a reserved, secured, reversed, or net amount.

A repeated outcome with the same status and reference returns `duplicate` after validation; a different reference conflicts. Otherwise, outcomes can change only from `requested` or `unknown`. Thus an unknown result can later be reconciled, while `completed` and `declined` cannot be replaced by another outcome.

A newly accepted outcome updates `/bankTransfer/status` and `/bankTransfer/reference` and emits `Transfer Outcome`. Completion additionally sets `/payment/completed` to the instruction amount, sets `/payment/transactionId` to the bank reference, and emits Payment Completed with `amountCompleted`, `requestId`, `reference`, and `evidence: bankConfirmation`. Requested, unknown, and declined statuses do not establish transferred money.

Missing state is unknown, not an implicit `idle`, false, zero, or completion. Detailed connection planning and the `requireActive` admission checks preceding contract operations are not supplied here; callable actions alone do not establish a person’s permission or obligation.
